architecture.description: The FE plans SQL, chooses fragment boundaries and destinations, and sends a TExecPlanFragmentParams request to each compute node. Its FILES() cardinality estimate is separate from the stream cardinality later declared to DuckDB. Bad FE estimates can choose a large shuffle before the CN sees the plan.
architecture.title: StarRocks FE

architecture.description: Descriptor tables map slot IDs to field positions and types. The translator lowers scans, exchanges, joins, expressions and aggregation phases into Substrait. An exchange becomes a read of sirius_stream_<id>. Partial and final aggregation must agree on the intermediate wire schema; AVG expands to sum and count.
architecture.title: Rust translator

architecture.description: The Rust Fragment<'ctx> wrapper calls the C++ Fragment API. Declared streams become bind-time views with schema and optional row estimates. lower_substrait owns a transaction when needed for catalog lookup and optimization. Sirius then converts the DuckDB logical plan into GPU operators.
architecture.title: DuckDB binding

architecture.description: The physical planner builds operators and pipeline boundaries. Tasks run cuDF/GPU work and use cuCascade memory tiers. Repository-backed streaming sources become ready when data arrives; sinks publish partitioned output and close only on completion. Stream queues deliberately have no byte-credit backpressure.
architecture.title: Sirius pipelines

architecture.description: The CN tracks local and remote destinations. A sender parks output; remote drains pack a batch into the sender arena, request a receiver lease, and execute a NIXL WRITE. PRPC carries lease requests, metadata, sequence numbers and EOS. Eligible local leaf fragments can instead be fused into the receiver plan.
architecture.title: CN exchange

architecture.description: Before copying an arrival, the receiver claims its sequence number. A fresh frame becomes a pool-backed inbound ticket and releases its arena lease. Once every required sender is complete, the CN builds/runs the receiver and transfers tickets to its input streams. ResultStore serves the FE; query-scoped error propagation retires related state.
architecture.title: Receiver & result

findings.description: After the receiver grants a lease, write_and_wait may fail before transmit_packed announces that lease to the receiver lifecycle. The sender cleanup releases only its local export lease. The unannounced receiver allocation has no query/ticket association for cancellation to reclaim.
findings.evidence: nixl_transport.rs:687–695 grants the lease then returns early on WRITE error; :719–735 releases only batch.offset on the sender. There is no remote lease-abort call in that window. Independently reviewed twice; no fault-injected GPU run.
findings.fix: P06: add idempotent remote lease abort with an allocation identity and safe transfer quiescence. Inject a post-grant failure and prove receiver capacity is recovered before marking ready.
findings.title: A failed remote WRITE can permanently consume receiver arena space

findings.description: The shared Send + Sync InboundStore handle may outlive Context. stage snapshots a raw gpu_space pointer under a mutex, unlocks, then dereferences it for allocation and data-batch creation. Context::close nulls the pointer and destroys the engine without waiting for an already active stage.
findings.evidence: Interleaving: stage reads non-null pointer; Context closes and destroys memory manager; stage resumes at get_default_allocator. The second null check after the copy cannot protect the earlier dereference. Source-confirmed, not sanitizer-reproduced.
findings.fix: P16: retain an owning lifetime guard or count active stages and wait in close. Cover concurrent Context teardown with a deliberately paused stage and sanitizer/GPU execution.
findings.title: InboundStore::stage can outlive the GPU memory space it dereferences

findings.description: The comparator converts cells to float and treats d > tolerance as the only mismatch condition. A NaN produces NaN distance, for which the comparison is false, so an invalid result can be certified against a finite oracle.
findings.evidence: Temporary fixture: oracle value 1.0; query result nan. The real compare.py returns MATCH and exit 0. A normal wrong-cold/correct-warm fixture correctly exits 1. Both are recorded in research/benchmark-validation.md.
findings.fix: Follow-up required before #1738 is ready: handle non-finite values explicitly before relative error. Add NaN/finite and infinity cases so invalid numeric results fail the benchmark gate; the opened draft leaves this unfixed.
findings.title: NaN can pass the numeric oracle comparison as MATCH

findings.description: Each fresh frame leaves the arena and becomes a GPU-pool allocation. The receiver waits for all senders’ EOS, so inbound tickets can accumulate beyond pool capacity. These allocations are not bound to receive credits or downgrade-managed reservations in this commit.
findings.evidence: The branch checklist records q18/q21 failing while staging a roughly 520 MB inbound frame into a full pool. This is historical workload evidence, not a new benchmark. Source inspection confirms an arena-only grant and default-allocator copy.
findings.fix: P16 and follow-on admission/spill PRs: define receive credits, reservation ownership, bounded frames and progress under the EOS barrier. Non-ancestor work is a candidate implementation, not an already accepted fix.
findings.title: Pool copy-out removes the arena bottleneck but leaves unadmitted ingress

findings.description: row_groups_in_byte_range forms the unsigned endpoint with start + length without checking overflow. Substrait range fields can reach this helper without that validation, so a malformed range can become an empty scan instead of a useful error.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic reproduction: start=4, length=UINT64_MAX wraps end to 3; a valid row-group offset 8 is excluded. Normal FE ranges are not shown to emit this malformed input, so this is a boundary-validation issue.
findings.fix: #1696 / P01: reject an overflowing range before scan planning and add the overflow case beside the boundary ownership tests.
findings.title: A byte-range endpoint can wrap and silently own no row groups

GitHub's commit-to-pulls endpoint returns no open PR for any uncovered commit. After the original inventory, ten source commits were extracted into #1737, #1738 and #1739. stages.description: The engine retains the fragment output for its downstream destinations. A local relay can consume it without a network hop. For this remote destination, the transport asks the engine for the next packed batch.
stages.title: Park the sender output

stages.description: Fragment::export_packed leases aligned space and packs the batch into it. The packing stream is synchronized before transport can use the bytes. A zero-row batch carries metadata without leasing a payload region. The sender owns release of this local lease.
stages.title: Pack into the sender arena

stages.description: A PRPC lease request asks CN B for a contiguous byte range and obtains its offset and device address. This checks the arena’s free space. It does not reserve receiver GPU-pool capacity and it does not register a query-owned inbound ticket yet.
stages.title: Reserve a remote staging lease

stages.description: The NIXL agent writes between the two registered regions and waits for DONE. Bulk data and PRPC metadata follow separate paths. A failure after remote grant needs a cleanup handshake; the current sender releases its local lease but has no remote abort, which is a P1 finding.
stages.title: Write the device bytes with NIXL

stages.description: transmit_packed first classifies the sequence as fresh, duplicate or retired. A fresh payload is unpacked and deep-copied to ordinary GPU pool memory on the RPC path. After stream synchronization, CN B releases its arena lease and records a ticket. Duplicates do not touch reused arena bytes.
stages.title: Claim sequence, then copy and free

stages.description: The PRPC reply completes the frame handoff. The sender releases its export lease and advances the sequence. The receiver now owns the pool copy. Its arena can accept another frame while the ticket still consumes pool memory. Sender output retires only after its consumers finish draining.
stages.title: Acknowledge the frame; retain the backlog

stages.description: EOS closes the sender’s contribution; it is not equivalent to one frame being acknowledged. When all required senders are complete, the receiver takes each ticket via push_inbound. Cancelled or refused receivers must drop retained tickets. The engine then executes the fragment against its input repositories.
stages.title: Dispatch the receiver and consume tickets
